title: Close a swing-top bottle: swing the stopper onto the mouth, then drive the lever through its over-centre point while the other hand steadies the bottle
instruction: Close the swing-top bottle of lemonade.
context: Swing-top bottles hold homemade lemonade, kombucha and home brew, and small producers close them by hand (O*NET 51-9111.00). The lever is an over-centre toggle: it resists harder until it passes its centre, then snaps shut and clamps the stopper. The stopper must go on first, the lever must be pushed through its peak (let go short and it springs open), and the bottle must be steadied by the other hand, or the push knocks it over.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Layout A, layout B in brackets. A 200 mL green-glass swing-top bottle of lemonade (0.45 kg), base centred at x 28, y -2 [B: 29, -3], upright: 15 cm tall, body 5.6 cm across and 8.5 cm tall, neck 2.5 cm across, lip 2.8 cm. A steel wire bail pivots on a band round the neck 2.5 cm below the mouth (pivots either side along x), carrying a white porcelain stopper (2.3 cm across, 1.4 cm tall, red rubber washer, 18 g) and a steel lever (two 5 cm wire arms, 1.8 cm thumb paddle, 12 g). Open at the start: the stopper rests out beside the neck on the right (-y), 95 degrees from its seat; the lever is flipped back over the top, lying out to the left (+y), 212 degrees from closed. Closed: stopper on the mouth, lever down the right side of the neck. Both arms start in the raised ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Tools: the trial video and a protractor or phone level. Sealed: the lever passed its centre (35 degrees short of closed) with the stopper on the mouth (within 5 degrees of its seat) and is still over it. Tipped: the bottle tilts 30 degrees or more at any time. 0 for the whole trial if tipped. Otherwise 1.0 once it is sealed, standing upright (tilt under 10 degrees, base on the table) and both grippers are 3 cm or more from the lever's paddle, together for 2 s; 0.5 if at the end the stopper is on the mouth and the bottle stands upright; else 0.
reset_notes: Open the bottle: flip the lever back over the top to the left, and rest the stopper out beside the neck on the right. Stand it upright at its mark.
fidelity: Rigid bottle, stopper and lever, the last two hinged at the neck. The wire bail's coupling is a joint rule each step: with the stopper seated the lever is sprung open from 75 degrees short of closed (0.21 N m at the centre); past its centre it is driven shut and the stopper clamped; otherwise both swing freely. No liquid: the lemonade is drawn and its mass is in the bottle; a 30 degree tilt stands in for spilling.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (arms reached toward the bottle; stopper and lever untouched, bottle left open); demo: 1.0 (sealed, full score at step 665)
